BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r5.claim: The garden became like a fully harvested orchard with nothing left because fire consumed it; another view compares it to night because it was blackened.
BURSEVI:v10p87#2/r5.anchor: كالبستان الذي صرمت ثماره لم بحيث لم يبق فيها شيء

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r4.claim: Attributing the orchard’s destruction to God signals that the disaster arrived wholly unexpectedly and devastated it in an instant.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p432/r4.anchor: the calamity arrived without the slightest expectation that it would

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r1.claim: The calamity was so devastating that it miraculously reduced the orchard to nothing in a blink; ‘from your Lord’ reassures the Prophet amid Quraysh’s apparent ease.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r1.anchor: it was so devastating in nature that it miraculously routed the orchard to nothingness in the blink of an eye

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r2.claim: The parable answers those who call the Prophet possessed because they feel secure: punishment can ruin even plans fixed by pledges when people wake to carry them out.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r2.anchor: all of man’s schemes which he devises with the conviction of pledges and oaths are rendered to ruin

QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r14.claim: A calamity from heaven struck while the orchard owners slept and burned their fruits, leaving the garden like a harvested field.
QUSHAYRI:v3p342/r14.anchor: أرسل عليها من السماء آفة فأحرقت ثمارهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r1.claim: Al-ṣarīm means the orchard had become black like night.

FARRA:v3p174/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p174/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p174/r4.claim: God sent a fire that destroyed the garden; the sons first thought they had lost their way, then recognized that their own refusal to help the poor had brought the loss.
FARRA:v3p174/r4.anchor: فلم يروا شيئا إلا سوادا فقالوا: «إنا لضالون»

FARRA:v3p174/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p174/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p174/r8.claim: الصريم means the garden had become black as night.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives two explanations of ṣarīm: black ash in Khuzaʿa speech, or a known barren sand in Yemen.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r12.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the garden became ṣarīm because its good was cut off from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p241/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن: صرم عنها الخير، أي قطع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r1.speaker: الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r1.claim: Al-Thawrī says ṣarīm can mean dawn because the garden turned white like harvested crop.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r1.anchor: وقال الثوري: كالصبح من حيث ابيضت كالزرع المحصود.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r2.speaker: مورج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r2.claim: Murajj likens it to a sand dune separated from the main dune, barren of useful growth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r2.anchor: وقال مورج: كالرملة انصرمت من معظم الرمل، والرملة لا تنبت شيئا ينفع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r3.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash says it is like dawn separated from night.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r3.anchor: وقال الأخفش: كالصبح انصرم من الليل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r4.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad says it became like daylight, with nothing left in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r4.anchor: وقال المبرد: كالنهار فلا شيء فيها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r5.speaker: شمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r5.claim: Shamr says ṣarīm can mean either night or day, each separating from the other.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r5.anchor: وقال شمر: الصريم: الليل، والصريم: النهار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r6.speaker: الفراء والقاضي منذر بن سعيد وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r6.claim: They say the garden became like night because it blackened.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r6.anchor: القاضي منذر بن سعيد وجماعة: الصريم: الليل من حيث اسودت

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#2/r1.claim: One explanation is that the garden turned black like night, burned; both night and morning are called ṣarīm because each is separated from the other.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#2/r1.anchor: {فأصبحت كالصريم} أي سوداء كالليل محترقة. و "الليل" هو: الصريم؛ و "الصبح" أيضا: صريم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#2/r2.claim: Another explanation says its fruit was gone as though it had been cut and harvested.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#2/r2.anchor: ويقال: "أصبحت: وقد ذهب ما فيها من الثمر؛ فكأنه صرم" (3) أي قطع وجذ.

MAJAZ:v2p265/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p265/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p265/r1.claim: Ṣarīm means severed at night and may itself mean night; a tract of sand cut off from the main dunes is also called ṣarīmah.
MAJAZ:v2p265/r1.anchor: «فأصبحت كالصريم » (20) انصرم فى الليل وهو الليل وكل رملة انصرمت من معظم الرمل فهى الصريمة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r1.claim: The garden became like an orchard whose fruit had been cut away, leaving nothing; الصريم is a passive-form adjective.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r1.anchor: كالبستان الذي صرمت ثماره بحيث لم يبق فيها شيء ففعيل بمعنى مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains الصريم as black ash, or as a known barren stretch of sand in Yemen.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس كالرماد الأسود وهو بهذا المعنى لغة خزيمة وعنه أيضا الصريم رملة باليمن معروفة لا تنبت شيئا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r3.speaker: مؤرج
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r3.claim: Muʾarrij compares it to a severed stretch of sand that grows nothing useful.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r3.anchor: وقال مؤرج كالرملة انصرمت من معظم الرمل وهي لا تنبت شيئا ينفع

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r4.speaker: منذر والفراء وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r4.claim: Al-Mundhir, al-Farra, and others understand it as night: the garden was burnt and black like night.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r4.anchor: وقال منذر والفراء وجماعة الصريم الليل والمراد أصبحت محترقة تشبه الليل في السواد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r5.speaker: الثوري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r5.claim: Al-Thawri understands الصريم as morning, because the garden had whitened like harvested crops; some say both night and day bear the name because each ends the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p30#5/r5.anchor: وقال الثوري كالصبح من حيث ابيضت كالزرع المحصود

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r3.claim: كالصريم can mean a black, dark night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r3.anchor: {فأصبحت كالصريم} كالليل المظلم الأسود. قال الحسن: أي صرم منها الخير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r4.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the garden was stripped of its good fruit, leaving nothing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: أي صرم منها الخير فليس فيها شيء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r5.speaker: الأخفش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash derives الصريم from something cut off: night and dawn each separate from the other, so either may be called al-sarim.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r5.anchor: وقال الأخفش: كالصبح الصريم من الليل وأصل "الصريم" المصروم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas gives ‘black ashes’ as the meaning in the Khuzaima dialect.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p195/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كالرماد الأسود بلغة خزيمة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r4.claim: The garden became like a harvested orchard, a blackened night, a whitened dry day, or sand; الصريم can be passive فعيل or either night or day because each separates from its opposite.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:18-22/r4.anchor: { فأصبحت كالصريم } كالبستان الذي صرم ثماره بحيث لم يبق فيه شيء

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r1.claim: Al-ṣarīm means cut or harvested; reports also gloss it as black ash in Khuzayma speech or a known Yemeni sand.
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r1.anchor: والصريم: المقطوع، والمحصود. ونقلوا أنه الرماد الأسود بلغة خزيمة

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.anchor: أن هذه الجنة كانت لرجل صالح، حدودا قومه وبلده فقيل إنه من أهل اليمن

NAHHAS:v5p9/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p9/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p9/r17.claim: Ṣarīm means something cut off, like maṣrūm, just as qatīl means maqtūl.
NAHHAS:v5p9/r17.anchor: أي كالشيء المصروم المقطوع وصريم بمعنى مصروم مثل قتيل بمعنى مقتول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r8.claim: Al-sarim can mean trees stripped of fruit, something severed from its destination, a dark night, or black ash; the orchard was entirely ruined because the heirs sought everything and did not give charity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p104/r8.anchor: كالأشجار التي صرم عنها ثمرها أو كالشيء الذي انقطع ما بينه وبين قاصده

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r4.claim: Qatada says God's command came upon the garden at night while its owners slept, leaving it like the dark night; Qatr ibn Maymun agrees.
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {فطاف عليها طائف من ربك وهم نائمون}

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r5.claim: The Prophet warns that sin can cause lost knowledge, missed night prayer, and withheld provision, then says the owners lost their garden because of their sin.
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إياكم والمعاصي

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-sarim as the black night.

DURR-FULL:v8p251/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p251/r7.claim: In a dialogue with Nafi ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas says al-sarim means gold and cites an anonymous poem using the word al-sarim.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the garden became black like the night.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3366/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : كالصريم قال : مثل الليل الاسود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r11.claim: One interpretation takes الصريم as night, also a name for day because each cuts off the other; pairing it with أصبح creates antithesis.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r12.speaker: جذيمة أو خزيمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r12.claim: Another reported dialectal meaning of الصريم is black ash.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p81/r12.anchor: وقيل الصريم : الرماد الأسود بلغة جذيمة أو خزيمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r1.claim: A further reported meaning of الصريم is a known barren sand tract in Yemen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r1.anchor: وقيل الصريم : اسم رملة معروفة باليمن لا تنبت شيئا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r2.claim: He favors the word's many meanings because all of them can suit the verse; يصرمنها and الصريم also form paronomasia.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r2.anchor: وإيثار كلمة الصريم هنا لكثرة معانيها وصلاحية جميع تلك المعاني لأن تراد في الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r3.claim: The fāʾ in فتنادوا derives the call from their oath: at morning they summon one another to carry out the plan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r3.anchor: وفاء { فتنادوا } للتفريع على { أقسموا ليصرمنها مصبحين ، }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r12.claim: Accounts differ on the ruined garden's appearance: black, or white like a harvested, dried crop.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r12.anchor: فقيل: أصبحت سوداء، وقيل: بيضاء كالزرع اليابس المحصود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r16.claim: As the garden owners were punished in their orchard, Quraysh face punishment in their worldly life, while repentance remains open to survivors as it was for the brothers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r16.anchor: فكما حل بأولئك العقاب في جنتهم كذلك يحل بهؤلاء في جميع دنياهم وفي حياتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r23.speaker: الفراء ومنذر وجماعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r23.claim: Al-Farra, Mundhir, and others take الصريم as night because the garden became black.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r23.anchor: والصريم: قال الفراء ومنذر وجماعة: أراد به الليل من حيث اسودت جنتهم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r24.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r24.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r24.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri takes الصريم as dawn because the garden became white like harvested grain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r24.anchor: وقال آخرون: أراد به الصبح من حيث ابيضت كالحصيد، قاله سفيان الثوري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r25.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r25.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r25.claim: الصريم can name either night or day because each is severed from the other.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r25.anchor: والصريم، يقال لليل والنهار من حيث كل واحد منهما ينصرم من صاحبه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r26.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r26.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r26.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that الصريم means black ash in the language of Judhayma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r26.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الصريم، الرماد الأسود بلغة جذيمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r27.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r27.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r27.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say الصريم is a known barren sandy tract in Yemen, used as a comparison for the garden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349/r27.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وغيره: الصريم، رملة باليمن معروفة لا تنبت فشبه جنتهم بها.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#2/r2.speaker: الفراء، ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#2/r2.claim: Al-ṣarīm means night: the garden became black like night after burning; morning and night are each called ṣarīm because each cuts off from the other.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#2/r2.anchor: كالليل المسود قاله الفراء وكذلك قال ابن قتيبة أصبحت سوداء كالليل محترقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#2/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, all the fruit was gone, as though it had been cut off.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p336#2/r3.anchor: وقد ذهب ما فيها من الثمر فكأنه قد صرم أي قطع وجذ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r3.claim: A heavenly calamity struck while they slept and left the orchard like a black night, according to Ibn Abbas, or like dry harvested stubble, according to al-Thawri and al-Suddi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي كالليل الأسود. وقال الثوري، والسدي: مثل الزرع إذا حصد،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r4.claim: A Prophetic report warns that a sin can deprive a person of provision already prepared for him, and applies the warning to the garden owners’ lost crop.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p195/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إياكم والمعاصي، إن العبد ليذنب

JISHUMI:v10p7031/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r6.claim: Both dawn and night are called ṣarīm because each cuts off the one before it; aṣbaḥa means to enter the morning.
JISHUMI:v10p7031/r6.anchor: ويقال للصبح: صريم، والليل: صريم؛ لأن كل واحد يقطع عن صاحبه

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r3.claim: The loss of the fruit may have been punishment or a trial that served as a grace, since it led them to repent.
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r3.anchor: يجوز الوجهان: أن يكون عقوبة، وأن يكون لطفا؛ لذلك تابوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r14.claim: The garden became like black ashes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r14.anchor: أحدها : كالرماد الأسود , قاله ابن عباس . الثاني : كالليل المظلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r15.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r15.claim: The garden became like a dark night; a poem uses صريم for dark night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p66/r15.anchor: الثاني : كالليل المظلم , قاله الفراء , قال الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r1.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r1.claim: The cited verse uses صريم for a dark night that does not clear by dawn.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r1.anchor: تطاول ليلك الجون البهيم فما ينجاب عن صبح , صريم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r31.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r31.claim: The garden became like a plot whose fruit had been cut away.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r31.anchor: الثالث : كالمصروم الذي لم يبق فيه ثمر .

MUQATIL:68:17-27/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r4.claim: By morning the garden was black like night.
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r4.anchor: { فأصبحت كالصريم } [آية: 20] أصبحت يعنى الجنة سوداء مثل الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#8/r1.claim: The garden became like dark night because it burned black, or like dawn as a treeless white plain, or like a cut-off orchard deprived of fruit.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p269#8/r1.anchor: كالليل المظلم أي احترقت فاسودت أو كالصبح أي صارت أرضا بيضاء

QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r6.claim: If al-sarim means night, the garden was blackened; if it means day, its trees and crops had vanished and the soil was bare.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:17/r6.anchor: فإن كان أراد الليل فلاسوداد موضعها

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Farra, and others explain al-sarim as a dark night; the scorched garden became black like night.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r1.anchor: أي كالليل المظلم عن ابن عباس والفراء وغيرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r2.claim: A cited poem describes the dark night as long and unable to clear by dawn, illustrating the night sense of al-sarim.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r2.anchor: تطاول ليلك الجون البهيم فما ينجاب عن صبح بهيم

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas also says al-sarim means black ash, using a Khuzaymi dialect word.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r4.speaker: الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r4.claim: Al-Thawri says it means a harvested crop, with al-sarim understood as something cut down.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r5.claim: Hasan explains that its good was cut off, treating al-sarim as a passive form.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r5.anchor: صرم عنها الخير أي قطع فالصريم مفعول أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r6.speaker: المؤرج
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r6.claim: Al-Mu’arrij compares it to a patch of sand separated from a larger dune, where nothing useful grows.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r6.anchor: الرملة لا تنبت شيئا ينتفع به.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r7.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash says al-sarim is the morning separated from night.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r8.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad interprets it as daytime, when nothing remains in the garden.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r9.speaker: شمر
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r9.claim: Shammir says both night and day are called sarim because each separates from the other; one view derives the night name from darkness stopping activity.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r9.anchor: الصريم الليل والصريم النهار أي ينصرم هذا عن ذاك وذاك عن هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r10.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r10.claim: Al-Qushayri objects that night cannot be called sarim because it stops activity, since day is also called sarim.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:20/r10.anchor: وفي هذا نظر لأن النهار يسمى صريما ولا يقطع عن تصرف

ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p208/r2.claim: The garden became black as night.

RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r2.claim: Ṣarīm can mean cut off as a passive participle: burned trees resemble fruitless, cut trees; al-Ḥasan explains that all good had been cut away.
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r2.anchor: أي صرم عنها الخير فليس فيها شيء

RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r3.claim: Other explanations compare the barren, burned garden to an isolated mass of sand, or to dawn after it has broken from night and left the garden dry and bare.
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r3.anchor: الصريم من الرمل قطعة ضخمة تنصرم عن سائر الرمال وجمعه الصرائم

RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r4.claim: Another explanation says the burned garden became black like night; both night and day are called ṣarīm because each breaks off into the other.
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r4.anchor: والليل يسمى صريما وكذا النهار يسمى أيضا صريما

RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p78#2/r5.claim: Some say night is ṣarīm because darkness prevents activity, or because it cuts off sight.

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r6.claim: The Arabic kaʾl-ṣarīm, rendered “like a garden plucked,” can also mean “like the blackness of night.”
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r6.anchor: Like a garden plucked translates kaʾl-ṣarīm, which can also mean “like the blackness of night”

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r7.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r7.claim: The Prophet reportedly warned that disobedience can take away a servant’s sustenance, then recited this verse.
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r7.anchor: The Prophet reportedly said, “Avoid sins of disobedience. Verily, the servant commits sins

TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.claim: A divine visitor struck the garden while its owners slept; in Arabic a ṭāʾif ordinarily comes at night, though one may explicitly say it came by day.
TAB-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.anchor: طاف عليها أمر من أمر الله وهم نائمون

TAB-FULL:v23p175/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ṣarīm as night.

TAB-FULL:v23p175/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that ṣarīm means night, a view illustrated by the poetry cited in the heading.

TAB-FULL:v23p175/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r3.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r3.claim: Another view says al-Ṣarīm was a known place, a Yemeni land called Ḍarwān near Ṣanʿāʾ.
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: فأصبحت كأرض تدعى الصريم

TAB-FULL:v23p175/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says al-Ṣarīm was a known place in Yemen called Ḍarwān, six miles from Ṣanʿāʾ.
TAB-FULL:v23p175/r4.anchor: هي أرض باليمن يقال لها ضروان من صنعاء على ستة أميال

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r2.claim: A night visitation from God afflicted and surrounded the garden; it became like cut fruitless trees, a dark night after burning, or a barren patch of sand.
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r2.anchor: أي بلاء يطوف عليها ويحيط بها ليلا

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r3.claim: Sarim can mean trees stripped of fruit, a black night, or a piece of sand separated from other sand and unable to grow anything.
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r3.anchor: وهو الشجر المقطوع ثمره أو المعنى

TABRISI:68:17-33/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r1.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:68:17-33/r1.claim: One explanation says the garden became like a harvest whose fruit had all been cut away.
TABRISI:68:17-33/r1.anchor: الصريم المصروم ثماره أي المقطوع والمعنى أنها صارت كأن جميع ثمارها قطعت عن الجبائي

TABRISI:68:17-33/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r2.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:68:17-33/r2.claim: Another explanation is a place from which all good has been cut off.
TABRISI:68:17-33/r2.anchor: وقيل: الصريم الذي صرم عنه الخير فليس فيه شيء منه عن الحسن

TABRISI:68:17-33/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r3.speaker: مؤرج
TABRISI:68:17-33/r3.claim: A third interpretation compares it to sand cut off from the bulk of the dune.
TABRISI:68:17-33/r3.anchor: وقيل: كالصريم أي كالرملة انصرمت عن معظم الرمل عن مؤرج

TABRISI:68:17-33/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:17-33/r4.claim: In Khuzaymī dialect, it can mean black ashes.

THALABI:v10p16/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16/r10.claim: The garden became like a dark, black night.

THALABI:v10p16/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16/r11.claim: A cited line calls a long, dark night a ṣarim, illustrating the garden's blackened state.
THALABI:v10p16/r11.anchor: تطاول ليلك الجون البهيم … فما ينجاب عن صبح صريم

THALABI:v10p16/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16/r12.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p16/r12.claim: Hasan says the garden was cut off from goodness and had nothing left.
THALABI:v10p16/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن: صرم عنها الخير فليس فيها شيء

THALABI:v10p16/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16/r13.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p16/r13.claim: Ibn Kaysan compares the burned garden to a black jar.

THALABI:v10p16#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16#2/r1.claim: The continued gloss attributed to Ibn Zayd compares the garden to cut-off land.
THALABI:v10p16#2/r1.anchor: كالأرض المصرومة، الأخفش: كالصبح انصرم من الليل

THALABI:v10p16#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r2.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v10p16#2/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash interprets ṣarim as dawn cut off from the night.

THALABI:v10p16#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r3.speaker: المروج
THALABI:v10p16#2/r3.claim: Al-Murawwaj compares it to a patch of sand cut off from the larger mass of sand.
THALABI:v10p16#2/r3.anchor: وقال المروج: كالرملة انصرمت من معظم الرمل

THALABI:v10p16#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p16#2/r4.claim: Ṣarim basically means something cut off; both night and dawn are called ṣarim because each separates from the other.
THALABI:v10p16#2/r4.anchor: وأصل الصريم: المصروم، وكل شيء قطع من شيء فهو صريم

THALABI:v10p16#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p16#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p16#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says ṣarim means black ashes in the Khudhaym dialect.
THALABI:v10p16#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كالرماد الأسود بلغة حذيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r6.claim: Muqatil says a fire burned the orchard overnight until it became black like night; Ibn Abbas in Ata's report gives the same comparison, supported by al-Farra and al-Zajjaj.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: بعث نارا بالليل على جنتهم فأحرقتها حتى صارت سوداء، فذلك قوله: {وهم نائمون (19) فأصبحت كالصريم} قال: يعني أصبحت الجنة سوداء كالليل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says الصريم means the darkest part of the night, when a moonless month's last night is especially dark.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r7.anchor: كالليل. وهو قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء؛ يعني كالليل المظلم (¬2)، شبه سوادها بسواد الليل الدامس، وهو آخر ليالي الشهر، وهو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r8.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r8.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj support interpreting الصريم as darkness like night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r8.anchor: وهو آخر ليالي الشهر، وهو أشد ما يكون ظلمة. وهذا القول في الصريم هو قول الفراء والزجاج (¬3). قال شمر: الصريم: الليل، والصريم:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r9.speaker: شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r9.claim: Shammar says الصريم can mean either night or day, since each breaks away from the other.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r9.anchor: قال شمر: الصريم: الليل، والصريم: النهار (¬4)، ينصرم الليل من النهار والنهار من الليل. وعلى هذا الصريم بمعنى المصارم (¬5). وقال غيره: سمي الليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r10.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r10.claim: Another linguist derives الصريم for night from its darkness cutting off people's ability to move about, taking the word as an active form, though that fails to explain its use for day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا الصريم بمعنى المصارم (¬5). وقال غيره: سمي الليل صريما لأنه يقطع بظلمته عن التصرف. وعلى هذا هو فعيل بمعنى فاعل، وهو يبطل بالنهار.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r11.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r11.claim: Qatada reads الصريم as the orchard having been cut down, so it means what was cut off.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: {كالصريم} كأنها صرمت (¬8). وعلى هذا الصريم بمعنى # المصروم، أي: المقطوع ما فيه. وأبى عطاء هذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r12.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r12.claim: Ata rejects the cut-down explanation attributed to Ibn Abbas because fire would burn trees and not make the garden resemble a harvested orchard; it is closer to fruit cut off while trees remain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r12.anchor: ما فيه. وأبى عطاء هذا القول فروى عن ابن عباس: وليس يعني المصرومة، وذلك أن النار تحرق الأشجار فلا تشبه ما في ثمره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r13.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r13.claim: Al-Hasan says goodness was cut away from the garden, leaving nothing in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن: أي: صرم عنها الخير فليس فيها شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r14.speaker: المؤرج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r14.claim: Al-Muʾarrij says it was like a detached patch of sand.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r14.anchor: وقال المؤرج: كالرملة (¬3) انصرمت من معظم الرمل (¬4). وقال الأصمعي: الصريم من الرمل: قطعة ضخمة تنصرم عن سائر الرمل،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r15.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r15.claim: Al-Asmaʿi defines الصريم in sand as a large separated section called a صرائم; this makes the charred, fruitless orchard resemble a barren isolated dune.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r15.anchor: من معظم الرمل (¬4). وقال الأصمعي: الصريم من الرمل: قطعة ضخمة تنصرم عن سائر الرمل، وتجمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r16.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r16.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r16.claim: Al-Akhfash says الصريم means dawn cut off from night, noting that day itself is also called صريم.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p97/r16.anchor: وقال الأخفش: كالصبح انصرم من الليل (¬7). وقد ذكرنا أن النهار يسمى صريما.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:17-21/r4.claim: The orchard became black like a dark night.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r16.claim: By morning, the paradise-like orchard had become a sırım, a ruined and scorched husk.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#4/r16.anchor: Derhâl o cennet gibi bağ sabaha kadar sırıma dönüvermişti

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r1.claim: Sarīm means wholly cut or severed; it can describe cut fruit, a harvested field, a night portion, or barren sand.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r2.claim: A transmitted interpretation takes the orchard itself, rather than only its fruit, as cut from the roots and burned black like ash.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r2.anchor: o bağın meyvesinin değil, kendisinin kökünden kesilip yanmış, kül gibi karara kalmış olduğu mervîdir

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r3.claim: Their sworn plan came true, but to their harm and in an unforeseen way, not as they intended or by their own hand.
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r3.anchor: Demek ki yemin ettikleri fiil olmuştu, fakat gönüllerindeki gibi ve kendi elleriyle lehlerine değil

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Descriptors after a named person can be construed as insults or as ordinary adjectives; the opening example does not repeat the person or introduce an unfamiliar fact.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: تقول أتاني زيد الفاسق الخبيث لم يرد أن يكرره

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: The verse beginning قبح من يزني بعوف can take الآكل الأشلاء as an accusative insult, or as a genitive adjective agreeing with the preceding noun.

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Yunus reports that al-Farazdaq's lines about Jaʿīr's aunt and maternal aunt are insults, with the milking reference making the addressee understand the abuse.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: وزعم يونس أنه سمع الفرزدق ينشد

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: The Farazdaq descriptions can also begin a fresh phrase and agree with the first noun; this is valid Arabic.

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: The lines طليق الله لميمتن عليه ... ولا الحجاج عيني بنت ماء are parsed like وجوه قرود.

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Hasan ibn Thabit's comparison of bodies to mules and minds to sparrows enumerates qualities rather than insulting the people.

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Al-Khalil says Hasan's lines could also be read as an insult, with the descriptors accusative on an implied verb.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: وقال الخليل رحمه الله لو جعله شتما فنصبه

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: A descriptive name may be accusative on an implied verb without praise or blame; محصنا identifies a man named Muḥṣin, as if the speaker said أعني.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: فنصبه على أعني وهو فعل يظهر لأنه

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Compassionate expressions use words such as المسكين and البائس, but this usage does not extend to every adjective or noun.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: ومن هذا الترحم والترحم يكون بالمسكين والبائس ونحوه

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Al-Khalil permits مررت به المسكين as apposition, with an implied compassionate sense, like مررت به أخيك.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: وزعم الخليل أنه يقول مررت به المسكين على البدل

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Al-Khalil also allows raising المسكين as a new predication, such as المسكين هو, or pairing it with البائس أنت.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: رفعته من وجهين فقلت مررت به

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: The compassionate expression can instead be accusative on an implied verb, as in بنا تميما يكشف الضباب; these parses convey the same meaning.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: فما يترحم به يجوز فيه هذان الوجهان

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Another poetic parse treats المسكين as the object of an understood verb, as in لقيته عبد الله, and this pattern is common in poetry.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: وهذا بمنزلة لقيته عبد الله إذا أراد عبد الله

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Yunus parses مررت به المسكين as a circumstantial accusative, equivalent to مررت به مسكينا.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: وأما يونس فيقول مررت به المسكين على قوله

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Sībawayh rejects Yunus's circumstantial parse because a حال cannot carry the definite article; a better explanation treats the phrase as an implied verb and avoids qualifying a pronoun.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: وهذا لا يجوز لأنه لا ينبغي أن يجعله حالا

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: Al-Khalil allows إنه المسكين أحمق by ellipsis, as إنه هو المسكين أحمق, but Sībawayh calls this weak; the accusative can separate subject and predicate.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: إنه المسكين أحمق على الإضمار الذي جاز فى مررت

SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.claim: With first- or second-person referents in بي المسكين or بك المسكين مررت, apposition is unsuitable; use an accusative like بنا تميما or raise it as before.
SIBAWAYH:تقولأتانيزيدالفاسقالخبيثلميردأن.anchor: فلا يحسن فيه البدل لأنك إذا عنيت المخاطب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r1.claim: Calling something by its opposite can express an omen or hopeful anticipation: a bitten person is called safe, the thirsty 'soon watered,' and a deadly desert a place of escape.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r1.anchor: ومن المقلوب: أن يوصف الشيء بضد صفته للتطير والتفاؤل، كقولهم للديغ: سليم،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r2.claim: Opposite naming can intensify description: the sun is called dark for its brilliance, and a crow one-eyed for its sharp sight.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r2.anchor: وللمبالغة في الوصف، كقولهم للشمس: جونة، لشدة ضوئها. وللغراب: أعور، لحدة بصره.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r3.claim: Opposite labels can be mockery, as when a black man is called father of the white and a white man father of the black.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r3.anchor: وللاستهزاء، كقولهم للحبشي: أبو البيضاء. وللأبيض: أبو الجون.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r10.claim: Ṣarīm names both night and dawn; here it means black as night, since night and day each break away from the other.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r10.anchor: قال الله سبحانه: فأصبحت كالصريم (20) [القلم: 20] ، أي سوداء كالليل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r11.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r11.claim: Sadfah can mean either darkness or light because each veils the other as it arrives.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r11.anchor: وللظلمة: سدفة. وللضوء: سدفة. وأصل السدفة: السترة،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r12.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r12.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r12.claim: Ṣārikh can mean either the person crying for help or the helper who cries in response.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p118/r12.anchor: وللمستغيث: صارخ. وللمغيث: صارخ، لأن المستغيث يصرخ في استغاثته،

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r1.claim: The preposition bāʾ can stand for min; Arabs say they drank bāʾ a particular water meaning they drank from it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r1.anchor: تقول العرب: شربت بماء كذا وكذا، أي من ماء كذا.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r3.claim: The Hudhalī poet's clouds drank from seawater; the line witnesses bāʾ meaning min.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r3.anchor: شربن بماء البحر ثم ترفعت ... متى لجج خضر لهن نئيج

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r4.claim: ʿAntarah's line about drinking from the water of al-Daḥraḍayn is another example of bāʾ meaning min.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p301#2/r4.anchor: شربت بماء الدحرضين فأصبحت ... زوراء تنفر عن حياض الديلم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains al-ṣarīm as something gone, supporting the sense with a poetic usage.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كالذاهب. واستشهد له بقول الشاعر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r2.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the orchard as having become like a black night.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r2.anchor: مثل ما قاله الفراء في معنى الآية: كاليل الأسود

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says it became black as night; night and day are each called ṣarīm because each breaks away from the other.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r3.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة في تأويل المشكل: أي سوداء كالليل لأن الليل ينصرم عن النهار، والنهار ينصرم عن الليل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r4.speaker: النابغة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r4.claim: Al-Nābigha’s verse is cited as evidence that Arabs used the related aṣrām in a simile of dark night.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p424/r4.anchor: نعم أما سمعت بقول النابغة وهو يقول

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r1.speaker: الأصمعي وأبو حاتم السجستاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r1.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī takes al-ṣarīm as night; Abū Ḥātim says it can be night or day as either parts from the other, and can also mean something cut off.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r1.anchor: ذكره الأصمعي في (الأضداد) وقال: ومن الصريم الليل قوله تعالى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو الشيباني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī cites Zuhayr’s verse to support the interpretation of ṣarīm as night.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r2.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو الشيباني، وأنشد بيت زهير: يريد الليل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanations: dark night and, in another report, black ash.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r3.anchor: وأسند الطبري عن ابن عباس، قال: الليل المظلم. وعنه أيضاً: كالرماد الأسود

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r4.speaker: سفيان
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r4.claim: Sufyān interprets the orchard as harvested crop, taking ṣarīm to mean something cut down.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r4.anchor: وعن سفيان: كالزرع المحصود، فالصريم بمعنى المصروم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib relates ṣarm to severance and gives two readings: trees stripped of their fruit or trees blackened as if by burning; Ibn al-Athīr likewise glosses it as cutting.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r5.anchor: والراغب فسر الصرْم بالقطيعة. وقال في الآية: قيل: أصبحت كالأشجار الصريمة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r6.claim: She prefers the cutting or harvesting sense over ‘gone’: the context does not support swearing to make the garden disappear and finding it like something gone.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p425/r6.anchor: ونرى دلالة القطع في الصرم. وفي الهجر والقطيعة، وفي الصرم: البت، والصارم: القاطع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1011/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1011/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1011/r1.claim: Qur’anic words of non-Arabic origin had entered Arabic before revelation, were Arabized and absorbed into its grammar; the Qur’an introduced no foreign vocabulary into Arabic.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1011/r1.anchor: جميع الكلمات الواردة في القرآن الكريم دخلت في لسان العرب قبل الإسلام ودخلت في كلامهم وأعربوها وأصبحت عربية في الاستعمال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1011/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1011/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1011/r2.claim: Non-Arabic origins can be inferred from unfamiliar forms or consonant combinations such as dāl and zāy; those borrowed words nevertheless became Arabic in use.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1011/r2.anchor: الكلمات الأعجمية أوزانها ليست كأوزان العرب أو تجتمع فيها حروف الدال والزاي مثلاً

BAQILLANI:v1p39/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p39/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p39/r1.claim: An objection says humans cannot know whether jinn are unable to match the Qur’an: jinn may have subtle powers beyond human reach and might still be able to produce its like.
BAQILLANI:v1p39/r1.anchor: لا سبيل لنا إلى أن نعلم عجز الجن عن الإتيان بمثله وقد يجوز أن يكونوا قادرين على الإتيان بمثله

BAQILLANI:v1p39/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p39/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p39/r2.claim: The author answers that God’s report could establish the jinn’s inability; alternatively, the challenge reflects Arab beliefs about conversing with jinn and their reputed poetry.
BAQILLANI:v1p39/r2.anchor: قيل قد يمكن أن نعرف ذلك بخبر الله عز وجل وقد يمكن أن يقال إن هذا الكلام خرج على ما كانت العرب تعتقده

BAQILLANI:v1p39/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p39/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p39/r3.claim: The preserved jinn poems known to Arabs, including material attributed to Taʾabbaṭa Sharran, ʿUbayd ibn Ayyūb, and others, do not exceed human eloquence and may fall short; conversations with jinn in the prophets’ era remain possible.
BAQILLANI:v1p39/r3.anchor: وقد علمنا أن ذلك محفوظ عندهم منقول عنهم والقدر الذي نقلوه من ذلك قد تأملناه

BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r1.claim: Abū Bakr’s testament appoints ʿUmar and says that if he acts justly this is Abū Bakr’s judgment of him, but if he deviates Abū Bakr cannot know the unseen; it quotes a warning to wrongdoers.
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r1.anchor: هذا ما عهد أبو بكر خليفة رسول الله آخر عهده بالدنيا وأول عهده بالآخرة

BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r2.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf reports visiting Abū Bakr during his final illness; Abū Bakr said the pain of the Muhājirūn’s resentment over his choice of ʿUmar weighed on him even more.
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r2.anchor: وفي حديث عبد الرحمن بن عوف رحمة الله عليه قال دخلت على أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه في علته التي مات فيها

BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r3.claim: Abū Bakr warns the community against luxury in silk furnishings and soft bedding, saying that facing beheading outside a legal penalty is better than plunging into worldly temptations; ʿAbd al-Raḥmān reassures him that he governed well.
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r3.anchor: والله لتتخذن نضائد الديباج وستور الحرير ولتألمن النوم على الصوف الأذربي

BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة بن الجراح ومعاذ بن جبل
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and Muʿādh’s letter warns ʿUmar that he must deal justly with all classes, remember the Day when faces bow and hearts tremble, and beware a future of public brotherhood masking private enmity; they say they write only as counsel.
BAQILLANI:v1p137#3/r4.anchor: نسخة كتاب كتبه أبو عبيدة بن الجراح ومعاذ بن جبل إلى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنهم

BAQILLANI:v1p215/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r1.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s poetry cannot approach Qur’anic composition; his own images compare separation to the unreachable edge of a setting star and to east never meeting west.
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r1.anchor: كيف سبيله وكيف طريق سقوط منزلة عن منزلته نظم القرآن وأنه لا يلحظ بشعره غبار ذلك وهو إذا لحظ ذلك كان كما قال

BAQILLANI:v1p215/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r2.claim: After establishing the principle and examining Imruʾ al-Qays in detail, al-Bāqillānī says he need not discuss every poet or eloquent speaker: a little evidence indicates much.
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r2.anchor: لم نحتج إلى أن نتكلم على شعر كل شاعر وكلام بليغ والقليل يدل على الكثير

BAQILLANI:v1p215/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r3.claim: The Qur’an’s compositional style differs from every other style and surpasses them in arrangement, wisdom, and eloquence.
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r3.anchor: مباينة أسلوب نظم القرآن جميع الأساليب ومزيته عليها في النظم والترتيب وتقدمه عليها في كل حكمة وبراعة

BAQILLANI:v1p215/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r4.claim: Even those who rank al-Buḥturī above Ibn al-Rūmī or place them level cannot expect to rank al-Buḥturī above Imruʾ al-Qays and his peers.
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r4.anchor: تفضيله على ابن الرومي أو تسوية ما بينهما ما لا يطمع معه في تقديمه على امرئ القيس ومن في طبقته

BAQILLANI:v1p215/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r5.claim: Abū Nuwās is judged against contemporaries and peers; the differences among their poetry are slight.
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r5.anchor: أبو نواس إنما يعدل شعره بشعر أشكاله ويقابل كلامه بكلام أضرابه من أهل عصره وإنما يقع بينهم التباين اليسير والتفاوت القليل

BAQILLANI:v1p215/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r6.claim: Thinking that poetry as a genre can rival Qur’anic composition is an absurd fall, likened to being hurled from the sky and snatched away or carried to a distant place.
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r6.anchor: فأما أن يظن ظان أو يتوهم أن متوهم أن جنس الشعر معارض لنظم القرآن

BAQILLANI:v1p215/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r7.claim: Poets’ thoughts change through borrowing and imitation; the aims they share belong to a familiar, contested, well-traveled poetic convention.
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r7.anchor: خواطر يغير بعضها على بعض ويقتدي فيها بعض ببعض والغرض الذي يرمي إليه ويصح التوافي عليه في الجملة

BAQILLANI:v1p215/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r8.speaker: الحسين بن الضحاك
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r8.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḍaḥḥāk says he recited his qasida, which blends debauchery with piety, to Abū Nuwās.
BAQILLANI:v1p215/r8.anchor: عن الحسين بن الضحاك قال أنشدت أبا نواس قصيدتي التي فيها

BURHAN:v2p208/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p208/r1.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p208/r1.claim: One reported interpretation takes الصريم as like a bright day, emptied of everything.
BURHAN:v2p208/r1.anchor: قيل معناه كالنهار مبيضة لا شيء فيها

BURHAN:v2p208/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p208/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p208/r2.claim: Another reported interpretation takes الصريم as like a dark night, emptied of everything.

BURHAN:v2p208/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p208/r3.speaker: ابن القشيري
BURHAN:v2p208/r3.claim: Ibn al-Qushayri says a word with one sense is taken in that sense; with multiple senses, choose the apparent one when a clue favors it, seek clarification when senses conflict, and suspend judgment when equally possible senses cannot be combined.
BURHAN:v2p208/r3.anchor: وقال ابن القشيري في مقدمة تفسيره مالا يحتمل إلا معنى واحدا حمل عليه وما احتمل معنيين فصاعدا

ITQAN:v2p359/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p359/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p359/r1.claim: A gloss identifies الصريم as that which has gone or vanished; the excerpt begins to introduce a poetic witness but does not preserve its line.
ITQAN:v2p359/r1.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ كالصريم ﴾ قال الذاهب أما سمعت قول الشاعر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r1.claim: Jurjani distinguishes representations that establish the possibility of a strange, disputed meaning from familiar meanings whose existence needs no proof.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r1.anchor: أن لا يكون المعنى الممثل غريبا نادرا يحتاج في دعوى كونه على الجملة إلى بينة وحجة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r2.claim: The water-grabber simile describes a person's frustrated hope of enjoying Layla and attaining union with her.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r2.anchor: كقابض على الماء خانته فروج الأصابع

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r3.claim: For familiar, already credible meanings, representation does not prove possibility; it instead measures their degree, force, weakness, or extent.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r3.anchor: فإن التمثيل وإن كان لا يفيد فيه هذا الضرب من الفائدة فهو يفيد أمرا آخر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r4.claim: Moving a familiar description from reason to sensory experience reveals its degree, as comparison with a crow's palate conveys the intensity of blackness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r4.anchor: كقياس الشيء على الشيء في اللون مثلا كحنك الغراب تريد أن تعرف مقدار الشدة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r5.claim: The image of water escaping through fingers makes the failure palpable as complete: the person gains neither a little nor a great deal.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p104/r5.anchor: بلغ في خيبه ظنه وبوار سعيه إلى أقصى المبالغ وانتهى فيه إلى ابعد الغايات

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r1.claim: Poetry can reverse a comparison: one poet makes a chick resemble an old man, while Abū Nuwās also makes an old man resemble a chick in elegies for Khalaf al-Aḥmar.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r1.anchor: ثم يعكس فيشبه الفرخ بالشيخ كما قال أبو نواس يرثى خلف الأحمر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r2.claim: Abū Nuwās repeats the old-man-and-chick comparison in another poem of his elegy.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r2.anchor: وأعاده في قصيدة أخرى في مرثيته

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r3.claim: The ostrich's wings, moving with slackness, are compared to a tent whose ropes have been removed; calling its dismantler inept heightens their uneven, unsettled motion.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r3.anchor: ويشبه الظليم في حركة جناحيه مع إرسال لهما بالخباء المقوض

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r4.claim: ʿAlqama's tent comparison specifies an inept woman dismantling it to intensify the unevenness and disorder of the ostrich's movements.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r4.anchor: صعل كأن جناحيه وجؤجؤه بيت أطافت به خرقاء مهجوم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r5.claim: In Dhū al-Rumma's lines, البيض are ostrich eggs and سماوة means the visible form of a black ostrich, contrasted with the eggs' whiteness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r5.anchor: قالوا في تفسيره يعنى بالبيض بيض النعام ورفعنا أي أثرنا عن ظهورها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r6.claim: The comparison presents an ostrich flushed from its eggs as a collapsed tent, while جون means black here because the passage contrasts it with whiteness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r6.anchor: ثم شبه النعام في حال إثارته عن البيض بالخباء المقوض

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r7.claim: The cited line is also evidence that هجوم, from a transitive use of هجم, functions verbally and governs نفسَه in the accusative: it means he threw himself upon them.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r7.anchor: أنشده شاهدا على إعمال فعول عمل الفعل وذلك قوله هجوم عليها نفسه فنفسه منصوب بهجوم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r8.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r8.claim: The poet depicts the ostrich's fearful contradiction: it clings to its eggs, yet springs up at a slight stimulus such as seeing a distant shape.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r8.anchor: أن يصف الظليم في خوفه بأمرين متضادين بان يبالغ في الانكباب على البيض فعل من شأنه اللزوم والثبات

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r9.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r9.claim: Jurjani praises the final phrase about a distant shape appearing in the ostrich's eyes as exceptionally beautiful.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p189/r9.anchor: وقوله يرم في عينيه بالشبح كلام ليس لحسنه نهاية

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r1.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r1.claim: Abū Zakariyyā describes ب as a genitive preposition and lists uses for attachment, instrument, exchange price, oath, location, and augmentation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r1.anchor: قال أبو زكريا : الباء حرف جر يدخل على الاسم فيجره

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba says ب can mean من, as in the expression شربت بماء; Antarah's line is cited as evidence.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r2.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة : تكون الباء بمعنى ( من ) ، تقول العرب : شربت بماء كذا ، أي من ماء كذا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r3.claim: Antarah's verse uses باء in بماء as evidence for the preposition meaning من.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r3.anchor: قال عنترة : - شربت بماء الدحرضين فأصبحت … زوراء تنفر عن حياض الديلم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r4.claim: The preposition ب can mean عن; ʿAlqama's verse is cited as evidence.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r4.anchor: وتكون الباء بمعنى : عن . قال علقمة بن عبدة : - فإن تسألوني بالنساء فإنني … بصير بأدواء النساء طبيب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r5.claim: Ibn Aḥmar's verse is also cited in connection with ب meaning عن.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p208/r5.anchor: وقال ابن أحمر : - تسائل يا ابن أحمر من رآه … أعارت عينه أم لم تعارا
